title: Virtual Personas for Language Models via an Anthology of Backstories

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the age distribution of LLM-generated personas to U.S. Census data and evaluating the model's ability to approximate human survey responses across different age groups using Wasserstein distance and consistency metrics.

Comparing the gender distribution of LLM-generated personas to U.S. Census data and evaluating the model's ability to approximate human survey responses across different gender groups using Wasserstein distance and consistency metrics.

Comparing the racial and ethnic distribution of LLM-generated personas to U.S. Census data and evaluating the model's ability to approximate human survey responses across different racial groups using Wasserstein distance and consistency metrics.

Comparing the education and income distributions of LLM-generated personas to U.S. Census data and evaluating the model's ability to approximate human survey responses across different education levels using Wasserstein distance and consistency metrics.

Analyzing the semantic diversity of generated backstories using pairwise BERTScores and qualitative assessment to ensure the generated personas do not rely on stereotypical or prototypical caricatures of demographic groups.
